cards.text: Paul and Barnabas, two teachers sent out by the Holy Spirit, are on a journey, and John has come along as their helper (Acts 13:1-5). They set sail from Paphos and land in Perga in Pamphylia, where John leaves them. The text doesn't say why, friend, and I am NOT about to write his excuse note for him.

cards.question: John leaves Paul and his companions at Perga. Where does he go back to?

cards.text: Paul and Barnabas travel inland to Pisidian Antioch, walk into the synagogue on the Sabbath, and sit down. Two men sent out by the Holy Spirit, and they just take a seat like anybody else, while I'd be in the front row waving my mustache at everybody.

cards.question: After the reading from the Law and the Prophets, the synagogue leaders tell the two visitors to stay quiet.
The synagogue leaders send word to Paul and Barnabas, inviting them to speak. What do the leaders ask for?

cards.text: Paul stands up and motions with his hand. That's the move that means "Put the phones down, I've got something to say."

cards.question: Paul's first words call out two groups in the synagogue. Who are they?

answers.text: Men of Israel and Gentiles who fear God
Priests and Levites from the temple

cards.text: Paul starts WAY back. God chose their fathers, made them a great people in Egypt, and led them out of that land with an uplifted arm.

cards.question: Paul says God endured His people's conduct in the wilderness for about forty years.

cards.text: God vanquished seven nations in Canaan and gave their land to His people as an inheritance. All this took about 450 years, and Paul gets through it faster than I can explain what I did last Tuesday.

cards.question: After all this, God gave His people ___ until the time of Samuel the prophet.

cards.text: The people ask for a king, and God gives them Saul son of Kish, from the tribe of Benjamin, who rules forty years. Not the Saul who's also called Paul (Acts 13:9), friend, a DIFFERENT Saul, and after removing him, God raises up a new king.

cards.question: After removing Saul, God raises up a new king and calls him "a man after My own heart." Who is this king?
Paul says that from the descendants of one man, God has brought Israel the Savior Jesus, as He promised. Which man?

cards.text: Before Jesus arrives, John the Baptist (Matthew 3:1) preaches a baptism of repentance to all the people of Israel. Not the John who left at Perga, friend, because apparently that name came in a value pack.

cards.question: As John is completing his course, he says there's One coming after him whose sandals he isn't worthy to untie. John is saying he himself is that One.

cards.text: Paul tells them this message of salvation has been sent to THEM. Then he says the people of Jerusalem and their rulers didn't recognize Jesus, and in condemning Him they fulfilled the words of the prophets read every Sabbath.

cards.question: The people of Jerusalem and their rulers found no ground for a death sentence, yet they asked ___ to have Jesus executed.

cards.text: When they've carried out all that was written about Him, they take Him down from the tree and lay Him in a tomb. But God raised Him from the dead, and friend, THAT is the line this whole sermon has been baking toward.

cards.question: For many days after God raises Him, Jesus is seen by those who had traveled with Him from Galilee to Jerusalem.

cards.text: Paul says the good news is this: what God promised their fathers, He has fulfilled by raising up Jesus. Then he quotes a Psalm: "You will not let Your Holy One see decay."

cards.question: Paul says David served God's purpose in his own generation and then fell asleep. What happened to David's body?

answers.text: It was buried and saw decay
It was taken up to heaven
It was never buried at all

cards.question: Paul says the One God raised did not see decay, and through Jesus forgiveness of sins is proclaimed. Through Him, everyone who ___ is justified from everything the law of Moses could not justify them from.

cards.text: Paul doesn't wrap up with a polite little thank-you, friend. He ends with a warning: watch out that what the prophets said doesn't happen to you, words aimed at scoffers about a work God is doing in their days.

cards.question: The prophets' warning to scoffers is about a work God is doing in their days. What does it say about that work?

answers.text: They'd never believe it if told
They'd see it and turn back
It will be finished in a day

cards.text: The sermon's done, and Paul and Barnabas head for the door. But the people in that synagogue are not done with them.

cards.question: As Paul and Barnabas leave the synagogue, what do the people urge them to do?

answers.text: Write the message on a scroll

cards.text: After the synagogue is dismissed, many of the Jews and devout converts to Judaism follow Paul and Barnabas. Paul's got followers, and NOT the phone kind.

cards.question: Paul and Barnabas urge the people following them to continue in the ___ of God.

cards.text: On the following Sabbath, nearly the WHOLE city gathers to hear the word of the Lord. Friend, I live alone on a cookie planet, and my biggest crowd ever is me and the oven timer.

cards.question: But when the Jews see the crowds gathering for Paul, they are filled with ___.

cards.text: They blasphemously contradict what Paul is saying. You know that one person in the group chat who answers every single message with "Actually…"? That energy, but in person.

cards.question: Facing all that contradicting, Paul and Barnabas back down and give a quiet, careful answer.

cards.text: Paul and Barnabas tell these Jews it was necessary to speak the word of God to them first. But since they reject it and don't consider themselves worthy of eternal life, Paul and Barnabas are about to make a turn, and friend, I mean a HARD turn.

cards.question: Since the word is rejected, who do Paul and Barnabas say they will turn to now?
Paul and Barnabas say this is what the Lord commanded them. In the Lord's words, what has He made them?

cards.text: When the Gentiles hear this, they rejoice and glorify the word of the Lord. Somebody just told them the door is open, and they are NOT waiting to be asked twice.

cards.question: In Pisidian Antioch, all who were appointed for eternal life believe.
After all this, how far does the word of the Lord spread?

answers.text: No farther than the city gate

cards.text: But the Jews incite the religious women of prominence and the leading men of the city. Then they stir up persecution against Paul and Barnabas.

cards.question: What does the persecution in Pisidian Antioch do to Paul and Barnabas?

answers.text: Drives them out of the district
Puts them in the city jail

cards.question: In protest, Paul and Barnabas shake the ___ off their feet and go to ___.
As this part of the journey ends, the disciples are filled with joy and with the Holy Spirit.

cards.text: Filled with joy AND the Holy Spirit, friend, and the only thing that ever filled me up in that junk drawer was dust. Keep that apron on, because this journey is not over yet.
